prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Miami for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist for implants in Miami — the right provider depends on your clinical needs (single tooth, full-arch, bone grafting), who you feel comfortable with, and whether you want a specialist (oral surgeon, periodontist, prosthodontist) or a general dentist who places implants.

How to find the best doctor for you
- Choose the right type of clinician: 
  - Oral and maxillofacial surgeons and periodontists most often place implants and manage complex bone/grafting cases. 
  - Prosthodontists specialize in restoring implants and are a good choice when aesthetics/function of the crown/bridge is most important. 
  - Many excellent practices use a team approach (surgeon places the implant, prosthodontist/restorative dentist does the crown).
- Verify training and credentials: board certification, fellowship/diplomate status in implant organizations (AAID, ICOI), or specialty board certification (ABOMS for surgeons, American Board of Prosthodontics).
- Experience and case mix: ask how many implants they place per year and how many procedures like yours they’ve done.
- Technology and planning: look for CBCT 3D imaging, guided implant planning, and digital workflows — these reduce surprises and improve outcomes.
- Before/after photos and patient references: ask to see cases similar to yours and read independent reviews (Google, Healthgrades, Yelp).
- Communication and follow-up: the best clinicians clearly explain alternatives, risks, timelines (healing/grafting), and warranties/what’s covered if an implant fails.

Questions to ask at a consult
- How many implants like mine have you placed?
- Are you a specialist? Where did you train?
- Do you use CBCT scans and guided implant placement?
- What implant brand do you use and why?
- If bone grafting/sinus lift is needed, do you do it here?
- What is the total cost (surgery + abutment + crown) and financing options?
- What is your implant failure rate and what happens if an implant fails?
- Can I see before/after photos and patient testimonials?

How to find local, reputable providers in Miami
- Use professional directories: American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID) “Find a Dentist,” American Academy of Periodontology, American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons (AAOMS), and ADA “Find a Dentist.”
- Read independent patient reviews (Google, Healthgrades, Yelp) and check complaints with your state dental board.
- Ask your general dentist for a referral — many have trusted specialists they work with.

If you’d like, I can:
- Narrow recommendations if you tell me your Miami neighborhood or ZIP code, whether you need a single implant or full-arch, and if you prefer a specialist type or same-day/sedation options.
- Give a checklist to bring to a consultation or a sample list of top-rated practices if you want me to suggest names based on available public lists (I’ll need your permission to check current online listings).
